head: environment

label: p
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{p}
  	Let $(n,c,u,p)$ be a suitable weak solution of \eqref{che}--\eqref{bound}. For any $\gamma\in(0,\frac12]$, $\rho>0$, and $\epsilon_1\in(0,\frac{3}{\tilde{r}}-1)$ is sufficiently small, there exist a constant $C=C(\tilde{q},\tilde{r},\epsilon_1)$ such that
  	\begin{align}
  		D(\gamma\rho)\leq& C\gamma^{1+\epsilon_1}\Big[D_{\tilde{q},1}(\rho)+A_u(\rho)+E_u(\rho)+\rho\left(A_{\sqrt{n}}(\rho)+E_{\sqrt{n}}(\rho)\right)\nonumber\\
  		& \qquad\qquad+\left(A_u(\rho)+E_u(\rho)\right)^\frac12\Big]\nonumber\\
  		&+C\gamma^{-1}\left[A_u(\rho)+E_u(\rho)+\rho M_\phi\left(A_{\sqrt{n}}(\rho)+E_{\sqrt{n}}(\rho)\right)\right], \label{D_1}
  	\end{align}
  	and
  	\begin{align}
  		D(\gamma\rho)\leq& C\gamma^{1+\epsilon_1}\Big[D(\rho)+A_u(\rho)+E_u(\rho)+\rho\left(A_{\sqrt{n}}(\rho)+E_{\sqrt{n}}(\rho)\right)+\left(A_u(\rho)+E_u(\rho)\right)^\frac12\Big]\nonumber\\
  		&+C\gamma^{-1}\left[A_u(\rho)+E_u(\rho)+\rho M_\phi\left(A_{\sqrt{n}}(\rho)+E_{\sqrt{n}}(\rho)\right)\right]. \label{D_2}
  	\end{align}
  	\begin{proof}
  		We prove the boundary case first. Without loss of generality, by scaling we assume $\rho=1$. Fix once and for all a smooth domain
$\tilde B$ satisfying $B_{3/4}^+\subset\tilde B\subset B_1^+$,
and set $\tilde Q=(-1,0)\times\tilde B$. This leaves a fixed
geometric gap for the homogeneous Stokes estimate from
$Q_{3/4}^+$ to $Q_{1/2}^+$. Define $r^*$ via $\frac{1}{r^*}=\frac{1}{\tilde{r}}+\frac13<1$. H\"{o}lder's inequality implies
  		\begin{align*}
  			\|u\cdot\nabla u\|_{L_t^{\tilde{q}}L_x^{r^*}(Q^+)}\leq \|\nabla u\|_{L_t^2L_x^2(Q^+)}\|u\|_{L_t^{q_1}L_x^{r_1}(Q^+)},
  		\end{align*}
  		where $\frac{1}{\tilde{q}}=\frac12+\frac{1}{q_1}$ and $\frac{1}{r^*}=\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{r_1}$.
  		Under the conditions on $(\tilde{q},\tilde{r})$, we have
  		\begin{align*}
  			&\frac{2}{\tilde{q}}+\frac{3}{r^*}=\frac{3}{\tilde{r}}+1+\frac{2}{\tilde{q}}=4,\\
  			&\frac{2}{\tilde{q}}+\frac{3}{r^*}=\frac{2}{q_1}+1+\frac{3}{r_1}+\frac32=4.
  		\end{align*}
  		Since $q_1\in(2,\infty)$, $r_1\in(2,6)$, and $\frac{2}{q_1}+\frac{3}{r_1}=\frac32$, Lemma \ref{interpolation} yields
  		\begin{align*}
  			\|u\cdot\nabla u\|_{L_t^{\tilde{q}}L_x^{r^*}(Q^+)}\leq C(A_u(1)+E_u(1)).
  		\end{align*}
  		Similarly,
  		\begin{align*}
  			\|n\|_{L_t^{\tilde{q}}L_x^{r^*}(Q^+)}\leq C\|n\|_{L_t^{\tilde{q}}L_x^{\tilde{r}}(Q^+)}= C\|\sqrt{n}\|^2_{L_t^{2\tilde{q}}L_x^{2\tilde{r}}(Q^+)}.
  		\end{align*}
  		Since $2\tilde{q}\in (2,4)$ and $2\tilde{r}\in (3,6)$, the scaling relation $\frac{2}{2\tilde{q}}+\frac{3}{2\tilde{r}}=\frac32$ holds. Thus,
  		\begin{align*}
  			\|n\|_{L_t^{\tilde{q}}L_x^{r^*}(Q^+)}\leq C(A_{\sqrt{n}}(1)+E_{\sqrt{n}}(1)).
  		\end{align*}
  		By Lemma \ref{stokes}, there exists a unique pair
  		\begin{align*}
  			v\in W^{1,2}_{\tilde{q},r^*}(\tilde{Q})\quad \text{and}\quad p_1\in W^{0,1}_{\tilde{q},r^*}(\tilde{Q})
  		\end{align*}
  		solving the initial boundary value problem:
  		\begin{align*}
  			\begin{cases}
  				\partial_tv-\Delta v+\nabla p_1=-u\cdot\nabla u-n\nabla\phi \quad&\text{in}~\tilde{Q},\\
  				\nabla\cdot v=0   &\text{in}~\tilde{Q},\\
  				[p_1]_{\tilde{B}}(t)=0 &\text{for almost everywhere (a.e.)}~t\in[-1,0],\\
  				v=0 &\text{on}~ \partial_p\tilde{Q}.
  			\end{cases}
  		\end{align*}
  		Moreover, the solution satisfies
  		\begin{align}
  			&\||v|+|\nabla v|+|p_1|+|\nabla p_1|\|_{L_t^{\tilde{q}}L_x^{r^*}(\tilde{Q})}\nonumber\\
  			\leq& C\left(\|u\cdot\nabla u\|_{L_t^{\tilde{q}}L_x^{r^*}(Q^+)}+\|\nabla\phi\|_{L^\infty_{t,x}(Q^+)}\|n\|_{L_t^{\tilde{q}}L_x^{r^*}(Q^+)}\right)\nonumber\\
  			\leq& C(A_u(1)+E_u(1))+C\|\nabla\phi\|_{L^\infty_{t,x}(Q^+)}(A_{\sqrt{n}}(1)+E_{\sqrt{n}}(1)). \label{E1}
  		\end{align}
  		The Sobolev-Poincar\'{e} inequality then yields
  		\begin{align}
  			&\|p_1\|_{L_t^{\tilde{q}}L_x^{\tilde{r}}(\tilde{Q})}\leq C\|\nabla p_1\|_{L_t^{\tilde{q}}L_x^{r^*}(\tilde{Q})}\nonumber\\ 
  			\leq&C(A_u(1)+E_u(1))+C\|\nabla\phi\|_{L^\infty_{t,x}(Q^+)}(A_{\sqrt{n}}(1)+E_{\sqrt{n}}(1)). \label{p_1}
  		\end{align}
  		Setting $w=u-v$ and $p_2=p-p_1$, the system for $(w, p_2)$ is
  		\begin{align*}
  			\begin{cases}
  				\partial_tw-\Delta w+\nabla p_2=0\quad &\text{in}~\tilde{Q},\\
  				\nabla\cdot w=0 &\text{in}~\tilde{Q},\\
  				w=0 &\text{on}~[-1,0)\times(\partial\tilde{B}\cap \{x_3=0\}).
  			\end{cases}
  		\end{align*}
  		Since $\tilde{q}\in (1,2)$, using \eqref{E1}, a simple calculation verifies that 
  		\[
  		w \in W^{0,1}_{\tilde{q}, 1}(\tilde{Q}) \quad \text{and}\; p_2 \in L^{\tilde{q}}_t L^1_x(\tilde{Q}).
  		\]
  		By H\"{o}lder's inequality, Sobolev-Poincar\'{e} inequality, and Lemma \ref{Seregin}, we obtain
  		\begin{align}
  			&\frac{1}{\gamma}\|p_2-[p_2]_\gamma\|_{L_t^{\tilde{q}}L_x^{\tilde{r}}(Q^+(\gamma))}\leq C\|\nabla p_2\|_{L_t^{\tilde{q}}L_x^{\tilde{r}}(Q^+(\gamma))}\nonumber\\
  			\leq & C\gamma^{3(\frac{1}{\tilde{r}}-\frac{1}{r'})}\|\nabla p_2\|_{L_t^{\tilde{q}}L_x^{r'}(Q^+(\gamma))}\leq C\gamma^{3(\frac{1}{\tilde{r}}-\frac{1}{r'})}\|\nabla p_2\|_{L_t^{\tilde{q}}L_x^{r'}(Q^+(\frac12))}\nonumber\\
  			\leq &C\gamma^{3(\frac{1}{\tilde{r}}-\frac{1}{r'})}\left(\|p_2-[p_2]_{\tilde{B}}\|_{L_t^{\tilde{q}}L_x^1(\tilde{Q})}+\|w\|_{L_t^{\tilde{q}}L_x^1(\tilde{Q})}\right)\nonumber\\
  			\leq & C\gamma^{3(\frac{1}{\tilde{r}}-\frac{1}{r'})}\left(D_{\tilde{q},1}(1)+\|p_1\|_{L_t^{\tilde{q}}L_x^1(\tilde{Q})}+\|v\|_{L_t^{\tilde{q}}L_x^1(\tilde{Q})}+\|u\|_{L_t^{\tilde{q}}L_x^1(Q^+)}\right)\nonumber\\
  			\leq &C\gamma^{3(\frac{1}{\tilde{r}}-\frac{1}{r'})}\Big[D_{\tilde{q},1}(1)+A_u(1)+E_u(1)+M_\phi\big(A_{\sqrt{n}}(1)+E_{\sqrt{n}}(1)\big)\nonumber\\
  			&\qquad\qquad\quad+ A_u(1)^{(\frac{1}{2\tilde{r}}-\frac{1}{6\tilde{q}})}E_u(1)^{\frac{1}{2\tilde{q}}}\Big], \label{p_2}
  		\end{align}
  		where $r'>\tilde{r}$ is arbitrary. Combining (\ref{p_1}) and (\ref{p_2}) yields
  		\begin{align*}
  			D(\gamma)\leq& C\gamma^{3(\frac{1}{\tilde{r}}-\frac{1}{r'})}\Big[D_{\tilde{q},1}(1)+A_u(1)+E_u(1)+M_\phi\big(A_{\sqrt{n}}(1)+E_{\sqrt{n}}(1)\big)\\
  			& \qquad\qquad\quad+\left(A_u(1)+E_u(1)\right)^\frac12\Big]\\
  			&+C\gamma^{-1}\Big[A_u(1)+E_u(1)+M_\phi\big(A_{\sqrt{n}}(1)+E_{\sqrt{n}}(1)\big)\Big].
  		\end{align*}
  		Rescaling this inequality gives
  		\begin{align*}
  			D(\gamma\rho)\leq& C\gamma^{3(\frac{1}{\tilde{r}}-\frac{1}{r'})}\Big[D_{\tilde{q},1}(\rho)+A_u(\rho)+E_u(\rho)+\rho M_\phi\big(A_{\sqrt{n}}(\rho)+E_{\sqrt{n}}(\rho)\big)\\
  			&\qquad\qquad\quad+\left(A_u(\rho )+E_u(\rho)\right)^\frac12\Big]\\
  			&+C\gamma^{-1}\left[A_u(\rho)+E_u(\rho)+\rho M_\phi\big(A_{\sqrt{n}}(\rho)+E_{\sqrt{n}}(\rho)\big)\right].
  		\end{align*}
  		Since $\tilde{r}<3$ and $r'$ can be chosen arbitrarily large, $\epsilon_1$ may range in $(0, \frac{3}{\tilde{r}} - 1)$. The force terms in the decaying bracket retain the
factor $\rho M_\phi$. To obtain the stated form of \eqref{D_1},
absorb these terms into the last bracket using
$\gamma^{1+\epsilon_1}\rho M_\phi
\leq\gamma^{-1}\rho M_\phi$; the additional nonnegative density
term in the first bracket may then be kept.
Finally, \eqref{D_2} follows from \eqref{D_1} and H\"older's inequality.

        We now consider the interior case. Fix an interior point
$z_0=(x_0,t_0)$ and an admissible radius $\rho$.
By translation and parabolic rescaling, we may assume that
$z_0=(0,0)$ and $\rho=1$, and retain the same notation for
the rescaled functions. We work on the full cylinder
$Q=(-1,0)\times B$, where $B=B_1$, using the notation
introduced in Section~\ref{subsec:notation-scaling}. In particular, all the
scale-invariant quantities below are evaluated on full
balls and cylinders.

For any spatially integrable function $f$, write
\[
[f]_r(t):=\frac{1}{|B_r|}\int_{B_r}f(x,t)\,dx.
\]
Let $\chi\in C_c^\infty(B)$ satisfy
\[
0\le\chi\le1,\qquad \chi\equiv1\quad\text{in }B_{3/4},
\]
and set $\bar u(t):=[u]_1(t)$ for almost every $t\in(-1,0)$.
Taking the divergence of the momentum equation and using
$\nabla\cdot u=0$, we have in the sense of distributions
\[
    -\Delta p
    =
    \partial_i\partial_j(u_i u_j)
    +
    \nabla\cdot(n\nabla\phi).
\]
Since $\bar u(t)$ is independent of $x$ and $\nabla\cdot u=0$,
\[
    \partial_i\partial_j
    \big((u_i-\bar u_i)(u_j-\bar u_j)\big)
    =
    \partial_i\partial_j(u_i u_j).
\]

For almost every fixed $t$, define on $\mathbb R^3$
\[
\begin{aligned}
p_1
={}&
(-\Delta)^{-1}\partial_i\partial_j
\Big[
\chi
(u_i-\bar u_i)(u_j-\bar u_j)
\Big]+
(-\Delta)^{-1}\nabla\cdot
\big(\chi n\nabla\phi\big),
\end{aligned}
\]
and put
\[
    p_2=p-p_1.
\]
Since $\chi\equiv1$ in $B_{3/4}$, comparison with the pressure
equation above yields
\[
    \Delta p_2=0
    \qquad\text{in }B_{3/4}
\]
for almost every $t\in(-1,0)$.

We first estimate $p_1$. Write
\[
    p_1=p_1^u+p_1^n,
\]
where $p_1^u$ and $p_1^n$ denote respectively the contributions of the
convective term and the external force. By the Calder\'on--Zygmund singular-integral estimate
(see Stein~\cite{Stein}),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\|p_1^u\|_
{L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}
((-1,0)\times\mathbb R^3)}
&\leq
C
\|(u-\bar u)\otimes(u-\bar u)\|_
{L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}(Q)}
=
C
\|u-\bar u\|_
{L_t^{2\tilde q}L_x^{2\tilde r}(Q)}^2.
\end{aligned}
\]
Since
\[
    \frac{2}{2\tilde q}
    +\frac{3}{2\tilde r}
    =\frac32,
\]
Lemma \ref{interpolation}, together with the Poincar\'e inequality, gives
\[
    \|u-\bar u\|_
    {L_t^{2\tilde q}L_x^{2\tilde r}(Q)}^2
    \leq
    C\big(A_u(1)+E_u(1)\big).
\]
Hence
\[
    \|p_1^u\|_
    {L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}
    ((-1,0)\times\mathbb R^3)}
    \leq
    C\big(A_u(1)+E_u(1)\big).
\]

For the contribution generated by $n\nabla\phi$, define
$\tilde r_*$ by
\[
    \frac1{\tilde r_*}
    =
    \frac1{\tilde r}+\frac13.
\]
Since $3/2<\tilde r<3$, one has
\[
    1<\tilde r_*<\frac32.
\]
The Hardy--Littlewood--Sobolev inequality
(see~\cite{Stein}) therefore yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
\|p_1^n\|_
{L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}
((-1,0)\times\mathbb R^3)}
&\leq
C
\|\chi n\nabla\phi\|_
{L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r_*}(Q)}
\leq
CM_\phi
\|n\|_
{L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r_*}(Q)}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Since $B$ has finite measure and
$\tilde r_*<\tilde r$,
\[
    \|n\|_
    {L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r_*}(Q)}
    \leq
    C
    \|n\|_
    {L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}(Q)}
    =
    C\|\sqrt n\|_
    {L_t^{2\tilde q}L_x^{2\tilde r}(Q)}^2
    \leq
    C\big(A_{\sqrt n}(1)+E_{\sqrt n}(1)\big).
\]
Consequently,
\[
    \|p_1^n\|_
    {L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}
    ((-1,0)\times\mathbb R^3)}
    \leq
    CM_\phi
    \big(A_{\sqrt n}(1)+E_{\sqrt n}(1)\big).
\]
Combining the preceding two estimates, we obtain
\[
\begin{aligned}
\|p_1\|_
{L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}
((-1,0)\times\mathbb R^3)}
\leq
C\Big[
A_u(1)+E_u(1)+
M_\phi\big(A_{\sqrt n}(1)+E_{\sqrt n}(1)\big)
\Big].
\end{aligned}
\]

It remains to estimate the harmonic part $p_2$. Since
$p_2(\cdot,t)$ is harmonic in $B_{3/4}$, the standard interior
estimate for harmonic functions implies
\[
    \|\nabla p_2(\cdot,t)\|_{L^\infty(B_{1/2})}
    \leq
    C
    \|p_2(\cdot,t)-[p_2]_{3/4}(t)\|_
    {L^1(B_{3/4})}.
\]
Hence, for every $\gamma\in(0,1/2]$,
the Poincar\'e inequality gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\|p_2-[p_2]_{\gamma}(t)\|_
{L^{\tilde r}(B_\gamma)}
\leq C\gamma\|\nabla p_2(\cdot,t)\|_{L^{\tilde{r}}(B_{\gamma})}\leq C\gamma^{1+\frac3{\tilde r}}\|\nabla p_2(\cdot,t)\|_{L^\infty(B_{1/2})}\\&\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\quad\leq
C\gamma^{1+\frac3{\tilde r}}
\|p_2-[p_2]_{3/4}(t)\|_
{L^1(B_{3/4})}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Taking the $L^{\tilde q}$ norm in time, and using
$(-\gamma^2,0)\subset(-1,0)$, we obtain
\[
\begin{aligned}
\|p_2-[p_2]_{\gamma}(t)\|_
{L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}(Q_\gamma)}
\leq
C\gamma^{1+\frac3{\tilde r}}
\|p_2-[p_2]_{3/4}(t)\|_
{L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^1
((-1,0)\times B_{3/4})}.
\end{aligned}
\]

Since $p_2=p-p_1$, the elementary estimate
\[
    \|f-[f]_{B_{3/4}}\|_{L^1(B_{3/4})}
    \leq
    2\|f-c(t)\|_{L^1(B_{3/4})}
\]
valid for every function $c(t)$, applied with
$c(t)=[p]_1(t)$, gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\|p_2-[p_2]_{3/4}(t)\|_
{L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^1
((-1,0)\times B_{3/4})}
\leq
C D_{\tilde q,1}(1)
+
C
\|p_1\|_
{L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}
((-1,0)\times\mathbb R^3)}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore,
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\frac1\gamma
\|p_2-[p_2]_{\gamma}(t)\|_
{L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}(Q_\gamma)}
\\&\leq{}
C\gamma^{\frac3{\tilde r}}
D_{\tilde q,1}(1)
+
C\gamma^{\frac3{\tilde r}}
\Big[
A_u(1)+E_u(1)
+
M_\phi\big(A_{\sqrt n}(1)+E_{\sqrt n}(1)\big)
\Big].
\end{aligned}
\]

For the localized part $p_1$, we simply use
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac1\gamma
\|p_1-[p_1]_{\gamma}(t)\|_
{L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}(Q_\gamma)}
&\leq
C\gamma^{-1}
\|p_1\|_
{L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}
((-1,0)\times\mathbb R^3)}
\\
&\leq
C\gamma^{-1}
\Big[
A_u(1)+E_u(1)
+
M_\phi\big(A_{\sqrt n}(1)+E_{\sqrt n}(1)\big)
\Big].
\end{aligned}
\]
Since $\gamma^{3/\tilde r}\leq\gamma^{-1}$ for
$0<\gamma\leq1/2$, combining the estimates for $p_1$ and $p_2$
gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
D(\gamma)
\leq{}
C\gamma^{\frac3{\tilde r}}
D_{\tilde q,1}(1)
+
C\gamma^{-1}
\Big[
A_u(1)+E_u(1)
+
M_\phi\big(A_{\sqrt n}(1)+E_{\sqrt n}(1)\big)
\Big].
\end{aligned}
\]

A standard parabolic rescaling now yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
D(\gamma\rho)
\leq{}
C\gamma^{\frac3{\tilde r}}
D_{\tilde q,1}(\rho)
+
C\gamma^{-1}
\Big[
A_u(\rho)+E_u(\rho)
+
\rho M_\phi
\big(A_{\sqrt n}(\rho)+E_{\sqrt n}(\rho)\big)
\Big].
\end{aligned}
\]
The factor $\rho$ in front of $\|\nabla\phi\|_{L^\infty}$ follows from
the rescaling
\[
    \phi_\rho(x)=\phi(\rho x),
    \qquad
    \|\nabla\phi_\rho\|_{L^\infty}
    =
    \rho\|\nabla\phi\|_{L^\infty}.
\]

Finally, H\"older's inequality in space and
$ \frac{2}{\tilde q}+\frac{3}{\tilde r}=3$
   give
\[
    D_{\tilde q,1}(\rho)
    \leq
    C D(\rho).
\]
Thus
\[
\begin{aligned}
D(\gamma\rho)
\leq{}
C\gamma^{\frac3{\tilde r}}D(\rho)
+
C\gamma^{-1}
\Big[
A_u(\rho)+E_u(\rho)
+
\rho M_\phi
\big(A_{\sqrt n}(\rho)+E_{\sqrt n}(\rho)\big)
\Big].
\end{aligned}
\]
Since $\tilde r<3$, one has $3/\tilde r>1$, and hence for
every $ 0<\epsilon_1<\frac3{\tilde r}-1$
and every $\gamma\in(0,1/2]$, $\gamma^{3/\tilde r}
    \leq
    \gamma^{1+\epsilon_1}$.
This proves the asserted interior pressure estimate.
  	\end{proof}

label: E1
title: Proof
body_md:
We prove the boundary case first. Without loss of generality, by scaling we assume $\rho=1$. Fix once and for all a smooth domain
$\tilde B$ satisfying $B_{3/4}^+\subset\tilde B\subset B_1^+$,
and set $\tilde Q=(-1,0)\times\tilde B$. This leaves a fixed
geometric gap for the homogeneous Stokes estimate from
$Q_{3/4}^+$ to $Q_{1/2}^+$. Define $r^*$ via $\frac{1}{r^*}=\frac{1}{\tilde{r}}+\frac13<1$. H\"{o}lder's inequality implies
  		\begin{align*}
  			\|u\cdot\nabla u\|_{L_t^{\tilde{q}}L_x^{r^*}(Q^+)}\leq \|\nabla u\|_{L_t^2L_x^2(Q^+)}\|u\|_{L_t^{q_1}L_x^{r_1}(Q^+)},
  		\end{align*}
  		where $\frac{1}{\tilde{q}}=\frac12+\frac{1}{q_1}$ and $\frac{1}{r^*}=\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{r_1}$.
  		Under the conditions on $(\tilde{q},\tilde{r})$, we have
  		\begin{align*}
  			&\frac{2}{\tilde{q}}+\frac{3}{r^*}=\frac{3}{\tilde{r}}+1+\frac{2}{\tilde{q}}=4,\\
  			&\frac{2}{\tilde{q}}+\frac{3}{r^*}=\frac{2}{q_1}+1+\frac{3}{r_1}+\frac32=4.
  		\end{align*}
  		Since $q_1\in(2,\infty)$, $r_1\in(2,6)$, and $\frac{2}{q_1}+\frac{3}{r_1}=\frac32$, Lemma \ref{interpolation} yields
  		\begin{align*}
  			\|u\cdot\nabla u\|_{L_t^{\tilde{q}}L_x^{r^*}(Q^+)}\leq C(A_u(1)+E_u(1)).
  		\end{align*}
  		Similarly,
  		\begin{align*}
  			\|n\|_{L_t^{\tilde{q}}L_x^{r^*}(Q^+)}\leq C\|n\|_{L_t^{\tilde{q}}L_x^{\tilde{r}}(Q^+)}= C\|\sqrt{n}\|^2_{L_t^{2\tilde{q}}L_x^{2\tilde{r}}(Q^+)}.
  		\end{align*}
  		Since $2\tilde{q}\in (2,4)$ and $2\tilde{r}\in (3,6)$, the scaling relation $\frac{2}{2\tilde{q}}+\frac{3}{2\tilde{r}}=\frac32$ holds. Thus,
  		\begin{align*}
  			\|n\|_{L_t^{\tilde{q}}L_x^{r^*}(Q^+)}\leq C(A_{\sqrt{n}}(1)+E_{\sqrt{n}}(1)).
  		\end{align*}
  		By Lemma \ref{stokes}, there exists a unique pair
  		\begin{align*}
  			v\in W^{1,2}_{\tilde{q},r^*}(\tilde{Q})\quad \text{and}\quad p_1\in W^{0,1}_{\tilde{q},r^*}(\tilde{Q})
  		\end{align*}
  		solving the initial boundary value problem:
  		\begin{align*}
  			\begin{cases}
  				\partial_tv-\Delta v+\nabla p_1=-u\cdot\nabla u-n\nabla\phi \quad&\text{in}~\tilde{Q},\\
  				\nabla\cdot v=0   &\text{in}~\tilde{Q},\\
  				[p_1]_{\tilde{B}}(t)=0 &\text{for almost everywhere (a.e.)}~t\in[-1,0],\\
  				v=0 &\text{on}~ \partial_p\tilde{Q}.
  			\end{cases}
  		\end{align*}
  		Moreover, the solution satisfies
  		\begin{align}
  			&\||v|+|\nabla v|+|p_1|+|\nabla p_1|\|_{L_t^{\tilde{q}}L_x^{r^*}(\tilde{Q})}\nonumber\\
  			\leq& C\left(\|u\cdot\nabla u\|_{L_t^{\tilde{q}}L_x^{r^*}(Q^+)}+\|\nabla\phi\|_{L^\infty_{t,x}(Q^+)}\|n\|_{L_t^{\tilde{q}}L_x^{r^*}(Q^+)}\right)\nonumber\\
  			\leq& C(A_u(1)+E_u(1))+C\|\nabla\phi\|_{L^\infty_{t,x}(Q^+)}(A_{\sqrt{n}}(1)+E_{\sqrt{n}}(1)). \label{E1}
  		\end{align}
  		The Sobolev-Poincar\'{e} inequality then yields
  		\begin{align}
  			&\|p_1\|_{L_t^{\tilde{q}}L_x^{\tilde{r}}(\tilde{Q})}\leq C\|\nabla p_1\|_{L_t^{\tilde{q}}L_x^{r^*}(\tilde{Q})}\nonumber\\ 
  			\leq&C(A_u(1)+E_u(1))+C\|\nabla\phi\|_{L^\infty_{t,x}(Q^+)}(A_{\sqrt{n}}(1)+E_{\sqrt{n}}(1)). \label{p_1}
  		\end{align}
  		Setting $w=u-v$ and $p_2=p-p_1$, the system for $(w, p_2)$ is
  		\begin{align*}
  			\begin{cases}
  				\partial_tw-\Delta w+\nabla p_2=0\quad &\text{in}~\tilde{Q},\\
  				\nabla\cdot w=0 &\text{in}~\tilde{Q},\\
  				w=0 &\text{on}~[-1,0)\times(\partial\tilde{B}\cap \{x_3=0\}).
  			\end{cases}
  		\end{align*}
  		Since $\tilde{q}\in (1,2)$, using \eqref{E1}, a simple calculation verifies that 
  		\[
  		w \in W^{0,1}_{\tilde{q}, 1}(\tilde{Q}) \quad \text{and}\; p_2 \in L^{\tilde{q}}_t L^1_x(\tilde{Q}).
  		\]
  		By H\"{o}lder's inequality, Sobolev-Poincar\'{e} inequality, and Lemma \ref{Seregin}, we obtain
  		\begin{align}
  			&\frac{1}{\gamma}\|p_2-[p_2]_\gamma\|_{L_t^{\tilde{q}}L_x^{\tilde{r}}(Q^+(\gamma))}\leq C\|\nabla p_2\|_{L_t^{\tilde{q}}L_x^{\tilde{r}}(Q^+(\gamma))}\nonumber\\
  			\leq & C\gamma^{3(\frac{1}{\tilde{r}}-\frac{1}{r'})}\|\nabla p_2\|_{L_t^{\tilde{q}}L_x^{r'}(Q^+(\gamma))}\leq C\gamma^{3(\frac{1}{\tilde{r}}-\frac{1}{r'})}\|\nabla p_2\|_{L_t^{\tilde{q}}L_x^{r'}(Q^+(\frac12))}\nonumber\\
  			\leq &C\gamma^{3(\frac{1}{\tilde{r}}-\frac{1}{r'})}\left(\|p_2-[p_2]_{\tilde{B}}\|_{L_t^{\tilde{q}}L_x^1(\tilde{Q})}+\|w\|_{L_t^{\tilde{q}}L_x^1(\tilde{Q})}\right)\nonumber\\
  			\leq & C\gamma^{3(\frac{1}{\tilde{r}}-\frac{1}{r'})}\left(D_{\tilde{q},1}(1)+\|p_1\|_{L_t^{\tilde{q}}L_x^1(\tilde{Q})}+\|v\|_{L_t^{\tilde{q}}L_x^1(\tilde{Q})}+\|u\|_{L_t^{\tilde{q}}L_x^1(Q^+)}\right)\nonumber\\
  			\leq &C\gamma^{3(\frac{1}{\tilde{r}}-\frac{1}{r'})}\Big[D_{\tilde{q},1}(1)+A_u(1)+E_u(1)+M_\phi\big(A_{\sqrt{n}}(1)+E_{\sqrt{n}}(1)\big)\nonumber\\
  			&\qquad\qquad\quad+ A_u(1)^{(\frac{1}{2\tilde{r}}-\frac{1}{6\tilde{q}})}E_u(1)^{\frac{1}{2\tilde{q}}}\Big], \label{p_2}
  		\end{align}
  		where $r'>\tilde{r}$ is arbitrary. Combining (\ref{p_1}) and (\ref{p_2}) yields
  		\begin{align*}
  			D(\gamma)\leq& C\gamma^{3(\frac{1}{\tilde{r}}-\frac{1}{r'})}\Big[D_{\tilde{q},1}(1)+A_u(1)+E_u(1)+M_\phi\big(A_{\sqrt{n}}(1)+E_{\sqrt{n}}(1)\big)\\
  			& \qquad\qquad\quad+\left(A_u(1)+E_u(1)\right)^\frac12\Big]\\
  			&+C\gamma^{-1}\Big[A_u(1)+E_u(1)+M_\phi\big(A_{\sqrt{n}}(1)+E_{\sqrt{n}}(1)\big)\Big].
  		\end{align*}
  		Rescaling this inequality gives
  		\begin{align*}
  			D(\gamma\rho)\leq& C\gamma^{3(\frac{1}{\tilde{r}}-\frac{1}{r'})}\Big[D_{\tilde{q},1}(\rho)+A_u(\rho)+E_u(\rho)+\rho M_\phi\big(A_{\sqrt{n}}(\rho)+E_{\sqrt{n}}(\rho)\big)\\
  			&\qquad\qquad\quad+\left(A_u(\rho )+E_u(\rho)\right)^\frac12\Big]\\
  			&+C\gamma^{-1}\left[A_u(\rho)+E_u(\rho)+\rho M_\phi\big(A_{\sqrt{n}}(\rho)+E_{\sqrt{n}}(\rho)\big)\right].
  		\end{align*}
  		Since $\tilde{r}<3$ and $r'$ can be chosen arbitrarily large, $\epsilon_1$ may range in $(0, \frac{3}{\tilde{r}} - 1)$. The force terms in the decaying bracket retain the
factor $\rho M_\phi$. To obtain the stated form of \eqref{D_1},
absorb these terms into the last bracket using
$\gamma^{1+\epsilon_1}\rho M_\phi
\leq\gamma^{-1}\rho M_\phi$; the additional nonnegative density
term in the first bracket may then be kept.
Finally, \eqref{D_2} follows from \eqref{D_1} and H\"older's inequality.

        We now consider the interior case. Fix an interior point
$z_0=(x_0,t_0)$ and an admissible radius $\rho$.
By translation and parabolic rescaling, we may assume that
$z_0=(0,0)$ and $\rho=1$, and retain the same notation for
the rescaled functions. We work on the full cylinder
$Q=(-1,0)\times B$, where $B=B_1$, using the notation
introduced in Section~\ref{subsec:notation-scaling}. In particular, all the
scale-invariant quantities below are evaluated on full
balls and cylinders.

For any spatially integrable function $f$, write
\[
[f]_r(t):=\frac{1}{|B_r|}\int_{B_r}f(x,t)\,dx.
\]
Let $\chi\in C_c^\infty(B)$ satisfy
\[
0\le\chi\le1,\qquad \chi\equiv1\quad\text{in }B_{3/4},
\]
and set $\bar u(t):=[u]_1(t)$ for almost every $t\in(-1,0)$.
Taking the divergence of the momentum equation and using
$\nabla\cdot u=0$, we have in the sense of distributions
\[
    -\Delta p
    =
    \partial_i\partial_j(u_i u_j)
    +
    \nabla\cdot(n\nabla\phi).
\]
Since $\bar u(t)$ is independent of $x$ and $\nabla\cdot u=0$,
\[
    \partial_i\partial_j
    \big((u_i-\bar u_i)(u_j-\bar u_j)\big)
    =
    \partial_i\partial_j(u_i u_j).
\]

For almost every fixed $t$, define on $\mathbb R^3$
\[
\begin{aligned}
p_1
={}&
(-\Delta)^{-1}\partial_i\partial_j
\Big[
\chi
(u_i-\bar u_i)(u_j-\bar u_j)
\Big]+
(-\Delta)^{-1}\nabla\cdot
\big(\chi n\nabla\phi\big),
\end{aligned}
\]
and put
\[
    p_2=p-p_1.
\]
Since $\chi\equiv1$ in $B_{3/4}$, comparison with the pressure
equation above yields
\[
    \Delta p_2=0
    \qquad\text{in }B_{3/4}
\]
for almost every $t\in(-1,0)$.

We first estimate $p_1$. Write
\[
    p_1=p_1^u+p_1^n,
\]
where $p_1^u$ and $p_1^n$ denote respectively the contributions of the
convective term and the external force. By the Calder\'on--Zygmund singular-integral estimate
(see Stein~\cite{Stein}),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\|p_1^u\|_
{L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}
((-1,0)\times\mathbb R^3)}
&\leq
C
\|(u-\bar u)\otimes(u-\bar u)\|_
{L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}(Q)}
=
C
\|u-\bar u\|_
{L_t^{2\tilde q}L_x^{2\tilde r}(Q)}^2.
\end{aligned}
\]
Since
\[
    \frac{2}{2\tilde q}
    +\frac{3}{2\tilde r}
    =\frac32,
\]
Lemma \ref{interpolation}, together with the Poincar\'e inequality, gives
\[
    \|u-\bar u\|_
    {L_t^{2\tilde q}L_x^{2\tilde r}(Q)}^2
    \leq
    C\big(A_u(1)+E_u(1)\big).
\]
Hence
\[
    \|p_1^u\|_
    {L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}
    ((-1,0)\times\mathbb R^3)}
    \leq
    C\big(A_u(1)+E_u(1)\big).
\]

For the contribution generated by $n\nabla\phi$, define
$\tilde r_*$ by
\[
    \frac1{\tilde r_*}
    =
    \frac1{\tilde r}+\frac13.
\]
Since $3/2<\tilde r<3$, one has
\[
    1<\tilde r_*<\frac32.
\]
The Hardy--Littlewood--Sobolev inequality
(see~\cite{Stein}) therefore yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
\|p_1^n\|_
{L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}
((-1,0)\times\mathbb R^3)}
&\leq
C
\|\chi n\nabla\phi\|_
{L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r_*}(Q)}
\leq
CM_\phi
\|n\|_
{L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r_*}(Q)}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Since $B$ has finite measure and
$\tilde r_*<\tilde r$,
\[
    \|n\|_
    {L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r_*}(Q)}
    \leq
    C
    \|n\|_
    {L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}(Q)}
    =
    C\|\sqrt n\|_
    {L_t^{2\tilde q}L_x^{2\tilde r}(Q)}^2
    \leq
    C\big(A_{\sqrt n}(1)+E_{\sqrt n}(1)\big).
\]
Consequently,
\[
    \|p_1^n\|_
    {L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}
    ((-1,0)\times\mathbb R^3)}
    \leq
    CM_\phi
    \big(A_{\sqrt n}(1)+E_{\sqrt n}(1)\big).
\]
Combining the preceding two estimates, we obtain
\[
\begin{aligned}
\|p_1\|_
{L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}
((-1,0)\times\mathbb R^3)}
\leq
C\Big[
A_u(1)+E_u(1)+
M_\phi\big(A_{\sqrt n}(1)+E_{\sqrt n}(1)\big)
\Big].
\end{aligned}
\]

It remains to estimate the harmonic part $p_2$. Since
$p_2(\cdot,t)$ is harmonic in $B_{3/4}$, the standard interior
estimate for harmonic functions implies
\[
    \|\nabla p_2(\cdot,t)\|_{L^\infty(B_{1/2})}
    \leq
    C
    \|p_2(\cdot,t)-[p_2]_{3/4}(t)\|_
    {L^1(B_{3/4})}.
\]
Hence, for every $\gamma\in(0,1/2]$,
the Poincar\'e inequality gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\|p_2-[p_2]_{\gamma}(t)\|_
{L^{\tilde r}(B_\gamma)}
\leq C\gamma\|\nabla p_2(\cdot,t)\|_{L^{\tilde{r}}(B_{\gamma})}\leq C\gamma^{1+\frac3{\tilde r}}\|\nabla p_2(\cdot,t)\|_{L^\infty(B_{1/2})}\\&\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\quad\leq
C\gamma^{1+\frac3{\tilde r}}
\|p_2-[p_2]_{3/4}(t)\|_
{L^1(B_{3/4})}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Taking the $L^{\tilde q}$ norm in time, and using
$(-\gamma^2,0)\subset(-1,0)$, we obtain
\[
\begin{aligned}
\|p_2-[p_2]_{\gamma}(t)\|_
{L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}(Q_\gamma)}
\leq
C\gamma^{1+\frac3{\tilde r}}
\|p_2-[p_2]_{3/4}(t)\|_
{L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^1
((-1,0)\times B_{3/4})}.
\end{aligned}
\]

Since $p_2=p-p_1$, the elementary estimate
\[
    \|f-[f]_{B_{3/4}}\|_{L^1(B_{3/4})}
    \leq
    2\|f-c(t)\|_{L^1(B_{3/4})}
\]
valid for every function $c(t)$, applied with
$c(t)=[p]_1(t)$, gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\|p_2-[p_2]_{3/4}(t)\|_
{L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^1
((-1,0)\times B_{3/4})}
\leq
C D_{\tilde q,1}(1)
+
C
\|p_1\|_
{L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}
((-1,0)\times\mathbb R^3)}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore,
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\frac1\gamma
\|p_2-[p_2]_{\gamma}(t)\|_
{L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}(Q_\gamma)}
\\&\leq{}
C\gamma^{\frac3{\tilde r}}
D_{\tilde q,1}(1)
+
C\gamma^{\frac3{\tilde r}}
\Big[
A_u(1)+E_u(1)
+
M_\phi\big(A_{\sqrt n}(1)+E_{\sqrt n}(1)\big)
\Big].
\end{aligned}
\]

For the localized part $p_1$, we simply use
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac1\gamma
\|p_1-[p_1]_{\gamma}(t)\|_
{L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}(Q_\gamma)}
&\leq
C\gamma^{-1}
\|p_1\|_
{L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}
((-1,0)\times\mathbb R^3)}
\\
&\leq
C\gamma^{-1}
\Big[
A_u(1)+E_u(1)
+
M_\phi\big(A_{\sqrt n}(1)+E_{\sqrt n}(1)\big)
\Big].
\end{aligned}
\]
Since $\gamma^{3/\tilde r}\leq\gamma^{-1}$ for
$0<\gamma\leq1/2$, combining the estimates for $p_1$ and $p_2$
gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
D(\gamma)
\leq{}
C\gamma^{\frac3{\tilde r}}
D_{\tilde q,1}(1)
+
C\gamma^{-1}
\Big[
A_u(1)+E_u(1)
+
M_\phi\big(A_{\sqrt n}(1)+E_{\sqrt n}(1)\big)
\Big].
\end{aligned}
\]

A standard parabolic rescaling now yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
D(\gamma\rho)
\leq{}
C\gamma^{\frac3{\tilde r}}
D_{\tilde q,1}(\rho)
+
C\gamma^{-1}
\Big[
A_u(\rho)+E_u(\rho)
+
\rho M_\phi
\big(A_{\sqrt n}(\rho)+E_{\sqrt n}(\rho)\big)
\Big].
\end{aligned}
\]
The factor $\rho$ in front of $\|\nabla\phi\|_{L^\infty}$ follows from
the rescaling
\[
    \phi_\rho(x)=\phi(\rho x),
    \qquad
    \|\nabla\phi_\rho\|_{L^\infty}
    =
    \rho\|\nabla\phi\|_{L^\infty}.
\]

Finally, H\"older's inequality in space and
$ \frac{2}{\tilde q}+\frac{3}{\tilde r}=3$
   give
\[
    D_{\tilde q,1}(\rho)
    \leq
    C D(\rho).
\]
Thus
\[
\begin{aligned}
D(\gamma\rho)
\leq{}
C\gamma^{\frac3{\tilde r}}D(\rho)
+
C\gamma^{-1}
\Big[
A_u(\rho)+E_u(\rho)
+
\rho M_\phi
\big(A_{\sqrt n}(\rho)+E_{\sqrt n}(\rho)\big)
\Big].
\end{aligned}
\]
Since $\tilde r<3$, one has $3/\tilde r>1$, and hence for
every $ 0<\epsilon_1<\frac3{\tilde r}-1$
and every $\gamma\in(0,1/2]$, $\gamma^{3/\tilde r}
    \leq
    \gamma^{1+\epsilon_1}$.
This proves the asserted interior pressure estimate.

head: environment
name: Pressure estimate at the exponent $5/3$

title: Proof
body_md:
By translation and parabolic rescaling, we first assume
$\rho=1$ and write $\gamma=r/\rho\le1/4$.
The local Sobolev inequality and interpolation give
\[
\|n\|_{L^{5/3}(\mathcal{Q})}
=
\|\sqrt n\|_{L^{10/3}(\mathcal{Q})}^2
\le
C\left[
A_{\sqrt n}(1)^{2/5}E_{\sqrt n}(1)^{3/5}
+A_{\sqrt n}(1)
\right].
\]
The last term is necessary because $\sqrt n$ has neither
zero trace nor zero spatial mean.


For a boundary cylinder, use the Stokes decomposition
from Lemma~\ref{p} with
\[
\tilde q=\tilde r=\frac53,
\qquad r_*=\frac{15}{14},
\qquad r'=\frac{15}{4}.
\]
The auxiliary fields $v,p_1$ are defined on $\tilde Q$ from
Lemma~\ref{p}; their global norms below are taken on this
domain. The original fields and forcing terms are estimated
on $\mathcal Q=Q_1^+$, and the smaller cylinders are contained
in $\tilde Q$.
Since $u=0$ on the flat boundary,
Sobolev--Poincar\'e interpolation yields
\[
\|u\cdot\nabla u\|_{L^{5/3}_tL^{15/14}_x(\mathcal{Q})}
\le C A_u(1)^{2/5}E_u(1)^{3/5},
\qquad
\|u\|_{L^{5/3}_tL^1_x(\mathcal{Q})}
\le C A_u(1)^{1/5}E_u(1)^{3/10}.
\]
Moreover,
\[
\|n\nabla\phi\|_{L^{5/3}_tL^{15/14}_x(\mathcal{Q})}
\le CM_\phi
\left[
A_{\sqrt n}(1)^{2/5}E_{\sqrt n}(1)^{3/5}
+A_{\sqrt n}(1)
\right].
\]
Applying the Stokes estimate to the localized problem,
with the preceding bounds for its forcing terms, gives
\begin{align*}
&\|p_1\|_{L^{5/3}(\tilde Q)}
+\|v\|_{L^{5/3}_tL^1_x(\tilde Q)}
\\
&\quad\le
C A_u(1)^{2/5}E_u(1)^{3/5}
+CM_\phi
\left[
A_{\sqrt n}(1)^{2/5}E_{\sqrt n}(1)^{3/5}
+A_{\sqrt n}(1)
\right].
\end{align*}
For the homogeneous remainder $(w,p_2)=(u-v,p-p_1)$,
the boundary Stokes estimate with $r'=15/4$ yields
\begin{align*}
\gamma^{-1}
\|p_2-[p_2]_\gamma\|_{L^{5/3}(\mathcal{Q}_{\gamma})}
\le C\gamma
\left[
\bar P(1)^{3/5}
+\|p_1\|_{L^{5/3}(\tilde Q)}
+\|v\|_{L^{5/3}_tL^1_x(\tilde Q)}
+\|u\|_{L^{5/3}_tL^1_x(\mathcal{Q})}
\right].
\end{align*}
Combining these estimates with
\[
\gamma^{-1}
\|p_1-[p_1]_\gamma\|_{L^{5/3}(\mathcal{Q}_{\gamma})}
\le
C\gamma^{-1}\|p_1\|_{L^{5/3}(\tilde Q)}
\]
and raising to the power $5/3$ proves the asserted
unit-scale estimate. Here the pure density term with
coefficient $\gamma^{5/3}$ is absorbed into its counterpart
with coefficient $\gamma^{-5/3}$.



For an interior cylinder, use the decomposition
$p=p_1^u+p_1^n+p_2$ from Lemma~\ref{p}.
The Calder\'on--Zygmund inequality and interpolation
for $u-[u]_1$ give
\[
\|p_1^u\|_{L^{5/3}(\mathcal{Q})}
\le C A_u(1)^{2/5}E_u(1)^{3/5}.
\]
The Hardy--Littlewood--Sobolev inequality gives
\begin{align*}
\|p_1^n\|_{L^{5/3}(\mathcal{Q})}
\le CM_\phi
\|n\|_{L^{5/3}_tL^{15/14}_x(\mathcal{Q})}
\le CM_\phi
\left[
A_{\sqrt n}(1)^{2/5}E_{\sqrt n}(1)^{3/5}
+A_{\sqrt n}(1)
\right].
\end{align*}
Since $p_2$ is harmonic in $B_{3/4}$, its interior
oscillation estimate implies
\begin{align*}
\bar P(\gamma)
\le C\gamma^3\bar P(1)
+C\gamma^{-5/3}
\Bigl[
A_u(1)^{2/3}E_u(1)
+M_\phi^{5/3}
\bigl(
A_{\sqrt n}(1)^{2/3}E_{\sqrt n}(1)
+A_{\sqrt n}(1)^{5/3}
\bigr)
\Bigr].
\end{align*}
This implies the asserted unit-scale estimate because
$\gamma^3\le\gamma^{5/3}$.

Rescaling back replaces $M_\phi$ by $\rho M_\phi$,
while $A$, $E$, and $\bar P$ remain invariant.
Using $\rho\le1$ and
\[
A_u^{2/3}E_u+A_{\sqrt n}^{2/3}E_{\sqrt n}
\le A_{u,\sqrt n}^{2/3}E_{u,\sqrt n}
\]
at radius $\rho$ completes the proof.

title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Choose 
\[
\epsilon_1
=
\min\left\{
\frac1{100},
\frac12\left(\frac3{\tilde r}-1\right)
\right\},
\qquad 
\eta=\epsilon_1^2,
\qquad 
\beta=\frac{\eta}{4},
\qquad 
\delta=\frac{\eta^2}{16},
\]
and set 
\[
l=\left\lceil\frac{12}{\epsilon_1}\right\rceil,
\qquad 
\tilde\beta=(1+\beta)^{l+1}-1.
\]
These parameters depend only on $\tilde q$, since 
\[
\frac2{\tilde q}+\frac3{\tilde r}=3.
\]
Moreover, Bernoulli's inequality and
\[
e^x-1
\leq\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}\frac{x^j}{j!}
\leq\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}x^j
=\frac{x}{1-x},
\qquad 0\leq x<1,
\]
give
\[
3\epsilon_1
\leq(l+1)\beta
\leq\tilde\beta
\leq e^{3\epsilon_1+\epsilon_1^2/2}-1
\leq4\epsilon_1.
\]

For an initial radius $\rho_0\in(0,1/2)$ to be chosen below, define
\[
\rho_k=\rho_0^{(1+\beta)^k},
\qquad k\geq0.
\]
We shall prove the stronger discrete estimates
\begin{equation}\label{4.11} 
A(\rho_k)+E(\rho_k)
\leq\frac14\rho_k^{2-\eta},
\qquad 
D(\rho_k)\leq\frac14\rho_k^{1+\eta}.
\end{equation} 
We first derive the inductive estimates, then choose $\rho_0$ and 
initialize the induction.

\par\medskip
\noindent
\textbf{Step 1. Inductive estimates.}\quad
Suppose that \eqref{4.11} holds for all indices
$0\le j\le k$, where $k\ge l$.
We take $\rho_0$ sufficiently small that the smallness
conditions in Corollaries~\ref{corollary1}
and~\ref{corollary2} hold at these scales and
$\rho_0^\beta\le1/2$.
The precise choice will be made in Step~2.

For the energy estimate, take $\gamma=\rho_k^\beta$.
Then $\gamma\rho_k=\rho_{k+1}$, and
Corollary~\ref{corollary1} gives
\begin{align*}
A(\rho_{k+1})+E(\rho_{k+1})
&\le
C_1\rho_k^{2\beta}
[A(\rho_k)+E(\rho_k)]^{1-\delta}
\\
&\quad+
C_1\rho_k^{-2\beta}
[A(\rho_k)+E(\rho_k)]^{3/2-\delta}
\\
&\quad+
C_1\rho_k^{-2\beta}
[A(\rho_k)+E(\rho_k)]^{1/2}D(\rho_k)
\\
&\le
C\left[
\rho_k^{2\beta+(2-\eta)(1-\delta)}
+
\rho_k^{-2\beta+(2-\eta)(3/2-\delta)}
+
\rho_k^{-2\beta+2+\eta/2}
\right].
\end{align*}
Here and below, the constants in the inductive estimates
are independent of $k$, $\rho_0$, and $\varepsilon_2$.
The required strict inequality between exponents is
\begin{equation}\label{4.12}
\begin{split}
\min\Bigl\{
&2\beta+(2-\eta)(1-\delta),\,
-2\beta+(2-\eta)(3/2-\delta),\\
&-2\beta+2+\eta/2
\Bigr\}
>
(2-\eta)(1+\beta).
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Indeed, subtracting the right-hand side from the three
exponents on the left gives, respectively,
\[
\beta\eta-(2-\eta)\delta
=\frac{\eta^2(2+\eta)}{16}>0,
\]
\[
(2-\eta)(1/2-\delta)-(4-\eta)\beta
=
1-\frac32\eta+\frac18\eta^2+\frac1{16}\eta^3>0,
\]
and
\[
\frac32\eta-(4-\eta)\beta
=
\frac12\eta+\frac14\eta^2>0.
\]

For the pressure estimate, we use the delayed scale
$\rho_{k-l}$, as in the iteration scheme of
\cite[Lemma 3.4]{DW2020}.
The definition of $\tilde\beta$ ensures that
\[
\rho_{k-l}^{1+\tilde\beta}=\rho_{k+1}.
\]
Thus we apply Corollary~\ref{corollary2} with
$\rho=\rho_{k-l}$ and
$\gamma=\rho_{k-l}^{\tilde\beta}$.
Since $\tilde\beta>\beta$, this scaling factor is also
at most $1/2$.
Using
$D_{\tilde q,1}(\rho)\le CD(\rho)$ and \eqref{4.11},
we obtain
\begin{equation}\label{eq:D_estimate}
D(\rho_{k+1})
\le
C\left[
\rho_{k-l}^{(1+\epsilon_1)\tilde\beta+1+\eta}
+
\rho_{k-l}^{(1+\epsilon_1)\tilde\beta+1-\eta/2}
+
\rho_{k-l}^{-\tilde\beta+2-\eta}
\right].
\end{equation}
The required pressure exponent condition is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:exponent_condition}
\begin{split}
\min\Bigl\{
&(1+\epsilon_1)\tilde\beta+1+\eta,\,
(1+\epsilon_1)\tilde\beta+1-\eta/2,\\
&-\tilde\beta+2-\eta
\Bigr\}
>
(1+\eta)(1+\tilde\beta).
\end{split}
\end{equation}
The corresponding exponent differences are
\[
(\epsilon_1-\eta)\tilde\beta,
\qquad
(\epsilon_1-\eta)\tilde\beta-\frac32\eta,
\qquad
1-2\eta-(2+\eta)\tilde\beta.
\]
They are all positive. In fact,
\[
(\epsilon_1-\eta)\tilde\beta-\frac32\eta
\ge
\left(\frac32-3\epsilon_1\right)\epsilon_1^2>0,
\]
and
\[
1-2\eta-(2+\eta)\tilde\beta
\ge
1-2\epsilon_1^2
-4\epsilon_1(2+\epsilon_1^2)>0.
\]
Here we used
$3\epsilon_1\le\tilde\beta\le4\epsilon_1$
and $0<\epsilon_1\le1/100$.

The strict exponent inequalities
\eqref{4.12} and \eqref{eq:exponent_condition} therefore
give, for some $\xi>0$ and $C_*>0$ independent of
$k$, $\rho_0$, and $\varepsilon_2$,
\[
A(\rho_{k+1})+E(\rho_{k+1})
\le C_*\rho_{k+1}^{2-\eta+\xi},
\qquad
D(\rho_{k+1})
\le C_*\rho_{k+1}^{1+\eta+\xi}.
\]

\par\medskip
\noindent
\textbf{Step 2. Choice of radius and initialization.}\quad
Fix $\rho_0\in(0,1/2)$ sufficiently small that
\[
\rho_0^\beta\le\frac12,
\qquad
C_*\rho_0^\xi\le\frac14,
\]
and that $\frac14\rho_0^{2-\eta}$ lies below the
smallness thresholds required in
Corollaries~\ref{corollary1} and~\ref{corollary2}.
This fixes all the radii $\rho_k$ before
$\varepsilon_2$ is chosen.

We now initialize \eqref{4.11} for $0\le j\le l$.
By \eqref{4.9}, domain inclusion gives
\[
A(1/2)+E(1/2)\le2\varepsilon_2.
\]
Applying Corollary~\ref{corollary2} at scale one
with $\gamma=1/2$, and taking $\varepsilon_2\le1$,
yields
\[
D(1/2)\le C_0\varepsilon_2^{1/2}.
\]
Consequently, for $0<r\le1/2$, domain inclusion
and comparison of the pressure averages give
\[
A(r)+E(r)\le\frac{\varepsilon_2}{r},
\qquad
D(r)\le\frac{C_0\varepsilon_2^{1/2}}{r},
\]
after enlarging $C_0$ if necessary.

Since $\rho_l\le\rho_j$ for $0\le j\le l$,
it suffices to choose $\varepsilon_2>0$ so small that
\[
\varepsilon_2\le\frac14\rho_l^{3-\eta},
\qquad
C_0\varepsilon_2^{1/2}
\le\frac14\rho_l^{2+\eta}.
\]
These inequalities imply \eqref{4.11} for
$j=0,\ldots,l$.

The estimates in Step~1 and
$C_*\rho_0^\xi\le1/4$ then show that, whenever
\eqref{4.11} holds up to an index $k\ge l$,
\[
A(\rho_{k+1})+E(\rho_{k+1})
\le\frac14\rho_{k+1}^{2-\eta},
\qquad
D(\rho_{k+1})
\le\frac14\rho_{k+1}^{1+\eta}.
\]
Thus \eqref{4.11} holds for every $k\ge0$.
All parameter choices depend only on
$\tilde q$, $M_c$, and $M_\phi$, so the same is true
of the resulting threshold $\varepsilon_2$.

\par\medskip
\noindent
\textbf{Step 3. Passage to arbitrary radii.}\quad
Let $0<r\le\rho_0$, and choose $k\ge0$ such that
\[
\rho_{k+1}<r\le\rho_k.
\]
By the definitions and domain inclusion,
\[
A(r)+E(r)
\le
\frac{\rho_k}{r}
\bigl(A(\rho_k)+E(\rho_k)\bigr)
\le
\frac{\rho_k^{3-\eta}}{4r}.
\]
For the pressure, comparison of spatial averages gives,
for almost every time,
\[
\|p-[p]_r\|_{L^{\tilde r}(B_r)}
\le
2\|p-[p]_{\rho_k}\|_{L^{\tilde r}(B_r)}
\le
2\|p-[p]_{\rho_k}\|_{L^{\tilde r}(B_{\rho_k})}.
\]
Restricting the time interval accordingly, we obtain
\[
D(r)
\le
2\frac{\rho_k}{r}D(\rho_k)
\le
\frac{\rho_k^{2+\eta}}{2r}.
\]
Since
$r>\rho_{k+1}=\rho_k^{1+\beta}$, it follows that
\[
A(r)+E(r)
\le
\frac14 r^{(3-\eta)/(1+\beta)-1}
\le r^{2-\eta_1},
\]
and
\[
D(r)
\le
\frac12 r^{(2+\eta)/(1+\beta)-1}
\le r^{1+\eta_2},
\]
where
\[
\eta_1=\frac{\eta+3\beta}{1+\beta}>0,
\qquad
\eta_2=\frac{\eta-2\beta}{1+\beta}>0.
\]
The positivity of $\eta_2$ follows from
$\beta=\eta/4$.
This proves \eqref{4.10}.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We use the normalized reference cylinders
$\mathcal Q_r=(-r^2,0)\times\mathcal B_r$
introduced in Section~\ref{subsec:notation-scaling}, and write $\mathcal Q=\mathcal Q_1$.
After a spatial translation and a time shift, we take the center
to be $(0,0)$; in the boundary case, the spatial translation
is tangential to $\Gamma$.

We first give the preliminary estimates common to both cases.
We then establish the local boundary estimates, treat the
interior case, and finally complete the boundary case
by a covering argument. For any integrable scalar- or vector-valued function $f$, set
\[
[f]_\rho:=\fint_{\mathcal Q_\rho}f(x,t)\,dx\,dt,
\]
where vector-valued averages are taken componentwise.
For the pressure, we retain the spatial-average notation
\[
[p]_\rho(t):=\fint_{\mathcal B_\rho}p(x,t)\,dx.
\]
Whenever the argument $t$ is omitted, $[p]_\rho$ still denotes
this time-dependent spatial average.
	   		 If the exponent in the statement satisfies $\tilde q\geq2$, set $q_*=3/2$.  Since the time interval has length one,
	   		 \[
	   		 \|p-[p]_1(t)\|_{L_t^{q_*}L_x^1(\mathcal{Q})}\leq
	   		 \|p-[p]_1(t)\|_{L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^1(\mathcal{Q})}.
	   		 \]
	   		 Thus the result for $q_*$ implies the stated result after decreasing the threshold.  It is therefore enough to prove the proposition for $1<\tilde q<2$, which is precisely the range used in the preceding pressure lemmas; $\tilde r\in(3/2,3)$ is then determined by $2/\tilde q+3/\tilde r=3$.
	   		 First, we observe that the smallness condition \eqref{14} in Proposition \ref{main1} implies the initial condition \eqref{4.9} of Lemma \ref{key}. Indeed, by the definitions of the scale-invariant quantities, the total energy at the unit scale satisfies
   		 \begin{align*}
   		 A_{u,\sqrt{n},\nabla \sqrt{\tilde{c}}}(1) + E_{u,\sqrt{n},\nabla \sqrt{\tilde{c}}}(1) + D_{\tilde{q},1}(1) \leq C \left( \varepsilon_0 + \varepsilon_0^{1/\tilde{q}} \right)
   		 \end{align*}
	   		 where $C=C(\tilde q,M_c,M_\phi)>1$. Therefore, by choosing $\varepsilon_0 = \varepsilon_0(\tilde{q},M_c,M_\phi) > 0$ sufficiently small such that $C ( \varepsilon_0 + \varepsilon_0^{1/\tilde{q}} ) \leq \varepsilon_2$, the condition \eqref{4.9} holds.

             We now consider the boundary case, so that
$\mathcal Q_r=Q_r^+$ and $\mathcal B_r=B_r^+$.
   		 Consequently, applying Lemma \ref{key}, we have the following estimates for $\rho \in (0, \rho_0]$:
   		\begin{align}\label{rho-estimate}
   			&\|p-[p]_{\rho}\|_{L_t^{\tilde{q}}L_x^{\tilde{r}}(Q^+_\rho)} \leq \rho^{2+\eta_2}, \quad \||u|^2\|_{L_t^{\tilde{q}}L_x^{\tilde{r}}(Q^+_\rho)} \leq C\rho^{3-\eta_1}, \nonumber\\
&\||\nabla\sqrt{\tilde{c}}|^2\|_{L_t^{\tilde{q}}L_x^{\tilde{r}}(Q^+_\rho)} \leq C\rho^{3-\eta_1}, \quad \|n\|_{L_t^{\tilde{q}}L_x^{\tilde{r}}(Q^+_\rho)} \leq C\rho^{3-\eta_1}.
   		\end{align}
The last three bounds also use Lemma~\ref{interpolation};
their constant $C$ depends only on the fixed parameters and is
independent of $\rho$.
    
    For $\rho\in(0,\rho_0]$ and each $i\in\{1,2,3\}$, put
$f^i=-n\partial_i\phi$ on $Q_\rho^+$.
Throughout the following construction, a superscript $*$,
placed after the component index, denotes the corresponding
function on the full ball or cylinder.

For almost every $t\in(-\rho^2,0)$, let $f^{i,*}$ be the odd
extension of $f^i$ across $\{x_3=0\}$, and let
$h^i\in W^{2,\tilde r}(B_\rho)\cap W_0^{1,\tilde r}(B_\rho)$
solve
\begin{equation}\label{eq:poisson}
    \Delta h^i=f^{i,*}\quad\text{in }B_\rho,
    \qquad h^i=0\quad\text{on }\partial B_\rho.
\end{equation}
Uniqueness and symmetry imply that $h^i$ is odd in $x_3$.
Set
\[
G^{i,*}:=\nabla h^i,
\qquad
G^i:=G^{i,*}|_{Q_\rho^+},
\qquad
G:=(G_j^i)_{i,j=1}^3.
\]
Then $\operatorname{div}G^i=f^i$ in $Q_\rho^+$.
Moreover, $G_1^{i,*}$ and $G_2^{i,*}$ are odd in $x_3$,
whereas $G_3^{i,*}$ is even.
The elliptic estimate, followed by integration in time, gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:force-divergence-bound}
    \|G\|_{L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}(Q_\rho^+)}
    \leq C\rho\|\nabla\phi\|_{L^\infty(Q_\rho^+)}
    \|n\|_{L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}(Q_\rho^+)}
    \leq C\|n\|_{L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}(Q_\rho^+)}.
\end{equation}

For each $i\in\{1,2,3\}$, define the vector field
$\mathcal F^i=(\mathcal F_j^i)_{j=1}^3$ on $Q_\rho^+$ by
\[
\mathcal F_j^i
=-u^iu^j-\delta_{ij}(p-[p]_\rho)+G_j^i.
\]
Let $\mathcal F^{i,*}$ be its extension to $Q_\rho$ obtained
by extending $\mathcal F_1^i,\mathcal F_2^i$ oddly and
$\mathcal F_3^i$ evenly across $\{x_3=0\}$.
Then $\operatorname{div}\mathcal F^{i,*}$ is odd in $x_3$
in the sense of distributions, and
\[
\|\mathcal F^{i,*}\|_{L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}(Q_\rho)}
\leq C
\|\mathcal F^i\|_{L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}(Q_\rho^+)}.
\]

Extend $\mathcal F^{i,*}$ by zero outside $B_\rho$ and define
\[
\omega^{i,*}:=\mathcal T_\rho\mathcal F^{i,*},
\qquad \omega^i:=\omega^{i,*}|_{Q_\rho^+},
\qquad \omega=(\omega^1,\omega^2,\omega^3),
\]
using Lemma~\ref{lem:heat-potentials}.
Then $\omega^{i,*}$ is odd and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:omega}
\partial_t\omega^i-\Delta\omega^i
=-\partial_j(u^iu^j)-n\partial_i\phi-\partial_i(p-[p]_\rho)
\quad\hbox{in }Q_\rho^+.
\end{equation}
In particular, \eqref{eq:heat-potential-div} gives directly
\begin{align}\label{omega}
\|\omega\|_{L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}(Q_\rho^+)}
&\leq C\rho\left(
 \||u|^2\|_{L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}(Q_\rho^+)}
 +\|p-[p]_\rho\|_{L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}(Q_\rho^+)}
 +\|G\|_{L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}(Q_\rho^+)}\right)\notag\\
&\leq C\rho(\rho^{3-\eta_1}+\rho^{2+\eta_2})
\leq C\rho^{3+\eta_2},
\end{align}
where $\eta_1+\eta_2<1$ and $\rho\leq1$.

Let $u^{i,*}$ be the odd extension of $u^i$, component by
component; no solenoidal property of this extension is required.
Its scalar momentum equation has right-hand side
$\operatorname{div}\mathcal F^{i,*}$ in $Q_\rho$.
Indeed, test the half-cylinder equation with the odd part of a
full-cylinder test function. That part vanishes on $\Gamma$;
the zero trace of $u^i$ removes the diffusion boundary term, and
the prescribed parities give exactly the reflected divergence.
The identity follows for the present weak solutions by approximation
of such zero-trace tests and the local integrability of
$\nabla u,u\otimes u,p,n$.
Thus $v^{i,*}=u^{i,*}-\omega^{i,*}$ is odd and caloric in $Q_\rho$.
In particular, its smooth interior representative vanishes on
the flat boundary. Writing $v=u-\omega$ and using
Lemma~\ref{lem:caloric-parity-decay}(i) with
$2/\tilde q+3/\tilde r=3$, we have
\begin{equation}\label{v}
\|v\|_{L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}(Q_\gamma^+)}
\leq C(\gamma/\rho)^4
\|v\|_{L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}(Q_\rho^+)},
\qquad 0<\gamma<\rho.
\end{equation}
This estimate uses the zero boundary value itself, so no subtraction
of an incompatible constant at $\Gamma$ is involved.

Combining \eqref{omega} and \eqref{v} gives
\[
\|u\|_{L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}(Q_\gamma^+)}
\leq C(\gamma/\rho)^4
\|u\|_{L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}(Q_\rho^+)}
+C\rho^{3+\eta_2}.
\]
The norm $\|u\|_{L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}(Q_{\rho_0}^+)}$
is bounded by \eqref{rho-estimate} and H\"older's inequality.
Lemma~\ref{it1}, since $3+\eta_2<4$, yields
\[
\|u\|_{L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}(Q_\gamma^+)}
\leq C\gamma^{3+\eta_2}.
\]


The mixed-norm bound for the averaging operator then implies
\begin{equation}\label{eq:u-campanato-decay}
\|u-[u]_\gamma\|_{L^1(Q_\gamma^+)}
\leq C\gamma^2\|u-[u]_\gamma\|_{L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}(Q_\gamma^+)}
\leq C\gamma^{5+\eta_2}.
\end{equation}



We next estimate $\nabla\tilde c=\nabla c$.
On $Q_\rho^+$ set
\[
g=-n\tilde c+n-u\cdot\nabla\tilde c.
\]
Extend $g$ evenly across $\Gamma$ and by zero outside $B_\rho$;
denote the resulting function by $g^*$. Define
\[
c_1^*=\mathcal S_\rho g^*,\qquad
c_1=c_1^*|_{Q_\rho^+},\qquad c_2=\tilde c-c_1.
\]
These definitions specify the auxiliary functions uniquely, without
requiring zero data on the artificial sphere. The even extension
$\tilde c^*$ satisfies
$(\partial_t-\Delta)\tilde c^*=g^*$ inside $Q_\rho$.
This follows by testing the weak scalar equation with the even
part of a full-cylinder test function. The weak Neumann condition
and $u=0$ on $\Gamma$ remove the boundary flux.
Consequently $c_2^*:=\tilde c^*-c_1^*$ is even and caloric,
and hence $\partial_3c_2^*=0$ on the flat boundary.

By \eqref{rho-estimate}, $1\leq\tilde c\leq M_c$, and
$\nabla\tilde c=2\sqrt{\tilde c}\nabla\sqrt{\tilde c}$,
\[
\begin{split}
\|g\|_{L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}(Q_\rho^+)}
\leq C(M_c)\left(
\|n\|_{L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}(Q_\rho^+)}
 +\||u|^2\|_{L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}(Q_\rho^+)}^{1/2}
  \||\nabla\sqrt{\tilde c}|^2\|_{L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}(Q_\rho^+)}^{1/2}
\right)\leq C\rho^{3-\eta_1}.
\end{split}
\]
The explicit gradient estimate \eqref{eq:heat-potential-scalar}
therefore gives
\[
\|\nabla c_1\|_{L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}(Q_\rho^+)}
\leq C\rho\|g\|_{L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}(Q_\rho^+)}
\leq C\rho^{4-\eta_1}.
\]

To preserve the boundary symmetry when subtracting constants, set
\[
\Phi_c(r)=\inf_{a\in\mathbb R^3,\ a_3=0}
 \|\nabla\tilde c-a\|_{L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}(Q_r^+)},
\qquad
\Phi_{c_2}(r)=\inf_{a\in\mathbb R^3,\ a_3=0}
 \|\nabla c_2-a\|_{L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}(Q_r^+)}.
\]
Lemma~\ref{lem:caloric-parity-decay}(ii) gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c2-gradient-decay}
\Phi_{c_2}(\gamma)
\leq C(\gamma/\rho)^4\Phi_{c_2}(\rho),
\qquad 0<\gamma<\rho.
\end{equation}
The triangle inequality, taking the infimum over $a_3=0$,
implies
\[
\Phi_c(\gamma)\leq\Phi_{c_2}(\gamma)+C\rho^{4-\eta_1},
\qquad
\Phi_{c_2}(\rho)\leq\Phi_c(\rho)+C\rho^{4-\eta_1}.
\]
Hence
\begin{equation}\label{eq:grad-c-campanato-iteration}
\Phi_c(\gamma)
\leq C(\gamma/\rho)^4\Phi_c(\rho)+C\rho^{4-\eta_1}.
\end{equation}
The initial value $\Phi_c(\rho_0)$ is bounded by taking $a=0$.
Since $4-\eta_1<4$, Lemma~\ref{it1} yields
$\Phi_c(\gamma)\leq C\gamma^{4-\eta_1}$.
For every admissible constant $a$ the ordinary averaging estimate gives
$\|\nabla\tilde c-[\nabla\tilde c]_\gamma\|
\leq2\|\nabla\tilde c-a\|$ in the same mixed norm.
Thus
\begin{equation}\label{eq:grad-c-mixed-campanato}
\|\nabla\tilde c-[\nabla\tilde c]_\gamma\|_
 {L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}(Q_\gamma^+)}
\leq2\Phi_c(\gamma)\leq C\gamma^{4-\eta_1},
\qquad 0<\gamma\leq\rho_0.
\end{equation}


Since
\[
	\frac{2}{\tilde q}+\frac{3}{\tilde r}=3,
\]
H\"older's inequality yields
\begin{align}
	\|\nabla\tilde c-[\nabla\tilde c]_{\gamma}\|_
	{L^1(Q_\gamma^+)}
	&\leq
	C\gamma^2
	\|\nabla\tilde c-[\nabla\tilde c]_{\gamma}\|_
	{L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}(Q_\gamma^+)}
	\nonumber\\
	&\leq C\gamma^{6-\eta_1}.
	\label{ccc}
\end{align}

We justify the uniformity in the center before applying
Campanato's characterization.
Recall that the reference cylinder in the present
boundary case is $Q_1^+(0,0)$.
For every boundary center
\[
z_b=((x_1,x_2,0),t),
\qquad |(x_1,x_2)|<1/8,\quad -1/64<t<0,
\]
we have
\[
Q_{1/2}^+(z_b)\subset Q_1^+(0,0).
\]
Write
\[
X(z,r):=
A_{u,\sqrt n,\nabla\sqrt{\tilde c}}(z,r)
+
E_{u,\sqrt n,\nabla\sqrt{\tilde c}}(z,r).
\]
By restriction to $Q_{1/2}^+(z_b)$ and comparison
of the spatial pressure averages, hypothesis \eqref{14} gives
\[
X(z_b,1/2)+D_{\tilde q,1}(z_b,1/2)
\leq C\bigl(\varepsilon_0+\varepsilon_0^{1/\tilde q}\bigr),
\]
with $C$ independent of $z_b$.
Choosing $\varepsilon_0$ sufficiently small, we may
therefore rescale each $Q_{1/2}^+(z_b)$ to a unit
half-cylinder and apply Lemma~\ref{key}, with the same
parameters and the same choice of $\rho_0$ for all
these centers.

Returning to the present coordinates, we obtain
\[
X(z_b,r)\leq Cr^{2-\eta_1},
\qquad
D(z_b,r)\leq Cr^{1+\eta_2},
\qquad 0<r\leq \rho_0/2,
\]
uniformly in $z_b$.

Repeating the preceding arguments gives, uniformly for the same
boundary centers and radii,
\[
\|u\|_{L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}(Q_r^+(z_b))}
\leq Cr^{3+\eta_2},\qquad
\inf_{a_3=0}\|\nabla\tilde c-a\|_
 {L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}(Q_r^+(z_b))}
\leq Cr^{4-\eta_1}.
\]
In particular, \eqref{eq:u-campanato-decay} and \eqref{ccc}
hold on these translated half-cylinders with common constants.


Fix
\[
0<\rho\leq \min\{1/8,\rho_0/6\},
\]
to be decreased further below if necessary.
For an interior center $z=(x,t)\in Q_\rho^+(0,0)$,
put
\[
d=x_3,\qquad s=d/2,\qquad
z_b=((x_1,x_2,0),t).
\]
Here $d$ is the distance to the flat boundary,
so $Q_s(z)$ is a full cylinder contained in the
half-space. Moreover,
\[
Q_s(z)\subset Q_{3s}^+(z_b),
\qquad
3s<3\rho/2\leq \rho_0/4.
\]
Thus the uniform boundary estimates apply at
the center $z_b$ and radius $3s$.
Comparison of the energy quantities and the
spatial pressure averages gives
\[
X(z,s)\leq Ks^{2-\eta_1},
\qquad
D(z,s)\leq Ks^{1+\eta_2},
\]
where $K$ is independent of the choice of
$z\in Q_\rho^+(0,0)$.

For $0<r\leq s$, all cylinders $Q_r(z)$ are full
interior cylinders.
Corollary~\ref{corollary1} applies whenever its
smallness condition holds, while the interior
pressure estimate in Lemma~\ref{p} gives
\[
D(z,\theta r)
\leq C\theta^{3/\tilde r}D(z,r)
+C\theta^{-1}X(z,r).
\]
The boundary comparison provides decay only at the
starting radius $s$.
To propagate this decay to $r<s$ with constants
independent of $s=d/2$, we repeat the induction
argument of Lemma~\ref{key}, retaining the above
powers of $s$ in the initial bounds.
Choose $\sigma>0$ sufficiently small that
\[
2\sigma<\eta_2,\qquad
\sigma(2+\eta_2)<1-\eta_1-\eta_2,
\]
and
\[
\sigma(4-\eta_1)
<
\min\left\{
\frac{2-\eta_1}{4},
\frac{\eta_1}{2}+\eta_2
\right\}.
\]
Then choose
\[
0<\delta<
\min\left\{
\frac14,
\frac{\sigma\eta_1}{2(2-\eta_1)}
\right\}.
\]
These choices are independent of the center $z$.
Since
\[
\eta_2<3/\tilde r-1,
\qquad \eta_1+\eta_2<1,
\]
the scale induction used in Lemma~\ref{key}, now with
$s_k=s^{(1+\sigma)^k}$ and the above interior pressure
estimate, yields
\[
X(z,s_k)\leq Ks_k^{2-\eta_1},
\qquad D(z,s_k)\leq Ks_k^{1+\eta_2}.
\]
Decrease $\rho$ so that the initial energy bounds
lie below the threshold in Corollary~\ref{corollary1},
$s^\sigma\leq 1/2$, and the positive powers of $s_k$
absorb the fixed constants in the induction.
This choice is independent of the center $z$.

Comparison of consecutive scales then gives, for $r\leq s$,
\[
X(z,r)\leq Cr^{2-\widehat\eta_1},
\qquad D(z,r)\leq Cr^{1+\widehat\eta_2},
\]
where
\[
\widehat\eta_1=\frac{\eta_1+3\sigma}{1+\sigma},
\qquad
\widehat\eta_2=\frac{\eta_2-2\sigma}{1+\sigma}.
\]
These exponents satisfy
$0<\widehat\eta_2<\eta_2$,
$\eta_1<\widehat\eta_1<1$, and
$\widehat\eta_1+\widehat\eta_2<1$.


For the interior cylinders $Q_r(z)$, $0<r\leq s$, use the same
heat potentials, with the data extended by zero outside the spatial
ball and without any reflection. For the force, solve the full-ball
Poisson problem in \eqref{eq:poisson} without taking an odd extension.
The remainders $v$ and $c_2$ are caloric in the full cylinder.
Define
\[
\Psi_f(z,r)=\left\|f-\fint_{Q_r(z)}f\right\|_
 {L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}(Q_r(z))}.
\]
The just-proved energy and pressure decay, Lemma~\ref{lem:heat-potentials},
and Lemma~\ref{lem:caloric-parity-decay}(iii), applied also to
the caloric vector $\nabla c_2$, imply
\[
\Psi_f(z,\gamma)
\leq C(\gamma/r)^4\Psi_f(z,r)+Cr^{3+\alpha},
\qquad 0<\gamma<r\leq s,
\]
where $(f,\alpha)=(u,\widehat\eta_2)$ or
$(\nabla\tilde c,1-\widehat\eta_1)$.
The initial bound at the moving radius $s=d/2$ is uniform:
restriction from $Q_{3s}^+(z_b)$ and the boundary mixed-norm estimates
give
\[
\Psi_f(z,s)\leq Cs^{3+\alpha_b},\qquad
\alpha_b=\eta_2\ \hbox{for }f=u,
\quad \alpha_b=1-\eta_1\ \hbox{for }f=\nabla\tilde c.
\]
In both cases $\alpha_b>\alpha$. Applying Lemma~\ref{it1} with
starting radius $s$ therefore yields
\[
\begin{split}
\Psi_f(z,r)
&\leq C(r/s)^{3+\alpha}\Psi_f(z,s)+Cr^{3+\alpha}\\
&\leq C(1+s^{\alpha_b-\alpha})r^{3+\alpha}
\leq Cr^{3+\alpha},\qquad 0<r\leq s<1.
\end{split}
\]
This explicitly proves that the oscillation constants do not
deteriorate as $d\downarrow0$.


For $r\geq d/2$, the same bound on
\[
\widehat Q_r(z)
:=(B_r(x)\cap\mathbb H^3)\times(t-r^2,t)
\]
follows from
$\widehat Q_r(z)\subset Q_{3r}^+(z_b)$
and the boundary oscillation estimates.
Fix $0<\rho_1<\rho/8$. On $Q_{\rho_1}^+$,
H\"older's inequality gives
\[
\int_{\widehat Q_r(z)}
\left|f-\fint_{\widehat Q_r(z)}f\right|\,dx\,dt
\leq Cr^{5+\alpha},
\]
uniformly in the center and in sufficiently small radii.
The parabolic Campanato characterization implies
\[
u\in C^{\widehat\eta_2,\widehat\eta_2/2}
(\overline{Q_{\rho_1}^+}),
\qquad
\nabla c=\nabla\tilde c
\in C^{1-\widehat\eta_1,(1-\widehat\eta_1)/2}
(\overline{Q_{\rho_1}^+}).
\]
The chosen $\rho_1$ depends only on the fixed parameters,
and the preceding estimates hold uniformly for
centers in $Q_{\rho_1}^+$ and all sufficiently
small radii.
For the remainder of the proof, we retain the notation
$\eta_1,\eta_2$ for the weaker exponents
$\widehat\eta_1,\widehat\eta_2$. Thus we have 
   		 \begin{align}\label{yj}
   		 \|u\|_{L^\infty_{t,x}(Q^+_{\rho_1})} + \|\nabla\tilde{c}\|_{L^\infty_{t,x}(Q^+_{\rho_1})} \leq C.
   		 \end{align}
   		We next estimate $n$.
Recall that \eqref{yj} gives uniform bounds for
$u$ and $\nabla\tilde c$ on $Q_{\rho_1}^+$.
Here and below, $\eta_1$ denotes the exponent retained
after the preceding interior estimates.

For $0<\rho\leq\rho_1/2$, put
$F=-n(u+\nabla\tilde c)$ on $Q_\rho^+$.
Extend $F_1,F_2$ evenly and $F_3$ oddly across $\Gamma$, then
extend the resulting field $F^*$ by zero outside $B_\rho$.
Set
\[
n_1^*=\mathcal T_\rho F^*,\qquad
n_1=n_1^*|_{Q_\rho^+},\qquad n_2=n-n_1.
\]
The even extension $n^*$ satisfies
$(\partial_t-\Delta)n^*=\operatorname{div}F^*$ in $Q_\rho$:
this is exactly the weak no-flux identity tested with even functions.
One may move the derivative of $n$ onto the test function because
its even part has zero normal derivative on $\Gamma$.
Thus $n_2^*:=n^*-n_1^*$ is even and caloric. This construction
uses no classical normal trace of $n$ or $F$ and imposes no
artificial spherical boundary data.
By \eqref{yj}, the density bound following from the energy decay,
and \eqref{eq:heat-potential-div},
\[
\begin{split}
\|n_1\|_{L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}(Q_\rho^+)}
\leq C\rho\|n(u+\nabla\tilde c)\|_{L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}(Q_\rho^+)}
\leq C\rho\|n\|_{L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}(Q_\rho^+)}
\leq C\rho^{4-\eta_1}.
\end{split}
\]


The even extension of $n_2$ solves the homogeneous
heat equation on the full cylinder $Q_\rho$.
Lemma~\ref{lem:caloric-parity-decay}(iii) therefore implies, for
$0<\gamma\leq\rho/2$,
\[
\|n_2-[n_2]_\gamma\|_
 {L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}(Q_\gamma^+)}
\leq
C\left(\frac{\gamma}{\rho}\right)^4
\|n_2-[n]_\rho\|_
 {L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}(Q_\rho^+)}.
\]
Using $n_2=n-n_1$ and the estimate for $n_1$, we obtain
\begin{align*}
\|n-[n]_\gamma\|_
 {L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}(Q_\gamma^+)}
&\leq
\|n_2-[n_2]_\gamma\|_
 {L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}(Q_\gamma^+)}
+2\|n_1\|_
 {L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}(Q_\gamma^+)}\\
&\leq
C\left(\frac{\gamma}{\rho}\right)^4
\|n-[n]_\rho\|_
 {L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}(Q_\rho^+)}
+C\rho^{4-\eta_1}.
\end{align*}
Applying Lemma~\ref{it1} with the fixed starting radius
$\rho_1/2$, and noting that $4-\eta_1<4$, yields
\[
\|n-[n]_\gamma\|_
 {L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}(Q_\gamma^+)}
\leq C\gamma^{4-\eta_1},
\qquad 0<\gamma\leq\rho_1/2.
\]
The constant may depend on the fixed radius $\rho_1$,
but is independent of $\gamma$.

Finally, since $2/\tilde q+3/\tilde r=3$,
H\"older's inequality gives
\begin{align}
\|n-[n]_\gamma\|_{L^1(Q_\gamma^+)}
&\leq
C\gamma^2
\|n-[n]_\gamma\|_
 {L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}(Q_\gamma^+)}
\leq C\gamma^{6-\eta_1}.
\label{nnn}
\end{align}

We spell out the uniformity for $n$ as well. For boundary centers
with $|x'|<\rho_1/8$ and $-\rho_1^2/64<t<0$, fix
$0<R_n\leq\rho_1/16$ small enough that the preceding uniform
energy bounds apply at all radii up to $R_n$. Their larger
cylinders lie in $Q_{\rho_1}^+$, where \eqref{yj} holds.
Repeating the preceding heat-potential argument gives the boundary
mixed-norm oscillation bound $Cr^{4-\eta_1}$ for $r\leq R_n$
with a common constant.
For an interior center $z$ in a sufficiently small fixed
half-cylinder, put $s=d/2$ and $a=\min\{s,R_n/3\}$.
If $s\leq R_n/3$, comparison with the boundary cylinder of radius
$3s\leq R_n$ gives $\Psi_n(z,a)\leq Ca^{4-\eta_1}$.
If $s>R_n/3$, the starting radius $a=R_n/3$ is fixed;
the uniform density norm then gives the same bound after changing
the constant, which may depend on $R_n$ but not on $z$.
On scales $r\leq a$, the full-cylinder heat-potential construction
and Lemma~\ref{lem:caloric-parity-decay}(iii) give
\[
\Psi_n(z,\gamma)
\leq C(\gamma/r)^4\Psi_n(z,r)+Cr^{4-\eta_1}.
\]
Here $\|n\|_{L_t^{\tilde q}L_x^{\tilde r}(Q_r(z))}
\leq Cr^{3-\eta_1}$ follows from the uniform energy decay above.
Lemma~\ref{it1} thus gives $\Psi_n(z,r)\leq Cr^{4-\eta_1}$
with a constant independent of $s$. For $s\leq r\leq R_n/3$,
restriction from the boundary cylinder of radius $3r$ gives the
same bound on the truncated cylinder. These two cases cover every
$0<r\leq R_n/3$. H\"older's inequality and Campanato's characterization
therefore give H\"older continuity of $n$ up to the boundary
on a fixed smaller half-cylinder.




 For an interior reference cylinder $Q_1$, we have
$Q_{1/4}(z)\subset Q_1$ for every $z\in Q_{1/2}$.
After decreasing $\varepsilon_0$ by a fixed factor,
Lemma~\ref{key} and the preceding full-cylinder
estimates give uniform oscillation decay at these
centers. Campanato's characterization therefore yields
H\"older continuity of $(n,\nabla c,u)$ in $Q_{1/2}$.

In the boundary case, cover $\overline{Q_{1/2}^+}$
by the closures of finitely many smaller boundary
half-cylinders and interior full cylinders, with
their larger cylinders contained in $Q_1^+$.
Fix this covering and decrease $\varepsilon_0$
so that, after rescaling, Lemma~\ref{key} applies
on every larger cylinder.
The local boundary and interior results proved above
then yield H\"older continuity of $(n,\nabla c,u)$
on $\overline{Q_{1/2}^+}$.

title: Proof

title: Proof
body_md:
Translate the normalized center to the origin. All constants
below may depend on $q,\tilde q,M_c,M_\phi$.
Write $\varepsilon$ for the left-hand side of
\eqref{eq:main2-smallness} and initially assume
$\varepsilon\leq1$. We use $C_M$ for constants that also depend
on the prescribed bound $M$, but not on the solution's entropy
or energy norms. They may be chosen nondecreasing in $M$ by
using $1+M$ in their upper bounds.

\medskip\noindent
\textit{Step 1: a mass-dependent local energy bound.}
Set
\[
\rho_k=\frac78-2^{-k-3},\qquad
X_k=A_{u,\sqrt n,\nabla\sqrt{\tilde c}}(\rho_k)
    +E_{u,\sqrt n,\nabla\sqrt{\tilde c}}(\rho_k),
\qquad k\geq0.
\]
In particular, $\rho_0=3/4$ and $\rho_k\uparrow7/8$.
Repeat the cutoff and pressure estimates in the proof of
Theorem~\ref{main3} on these nested cylinders, with its spatial
exponent equal to $q$. The pressure-exponent reduction made
there remains valid, since $F(q,q)=1$.
In those estimates, retain the bound $M$ for each density
$L^1$ factor and the bound $\varepsilon$ for the velocity,
signal-gradient, and pressure factors.

Here is the resulting control of the terms for which the
density smallness was previously used. With the interpolation
parameter $\tau_1$ of that proof and sufficiently small
$0<\alpha<\min\{2/5,\tau_1/5\}$, the estimates on each
$\mathcal Q_{\rho_{k+1}}$ give
\begin{align*}
\int n&\leq M,\qquad
\int n^{1-\alpha}\leq C M^{1-\alpha},\\
\int n^{1+\alpha}
&\leq C M^{1-3\alpha/2}X_{k+1}^{5\alpha/2},\\
\int n|u|
&\leq C\varepsilon M^{\tau_1/2}
X_{k+1}^{1-\tau_1/2},\\
\int n^{1+\alpha}|u|
&\leq C\varepsilon M^{(\tau_1-3\alpha)/2}
X_{k+1}^{1+5\alpha/2-\tau_1/2},\\
\int n^{1-\alpha}|u|
&\leq C\varepsilon M^{\tau_1(1-\alpha)/2}
X_{k+1}^{(1-\tau_1/2)(1-\alpha)}.
\end{align*}
All integrals in this display are space--time integrals.
The same estimates hold with $|u|$ replaced by $|\nabla c|$,
because
$|\nabla c|\leq2\sqrt{M_c}|\nabla\sqrt{\tilde c}|$.
The fractional power of the mass-flux integral in
\eqref{eq:section5-rhs} is controlled by the same bounds and
$(a+b)^{1-\alpha}\leq a^{1-\alpha}+b^{1-\alpha}$.

For completeness, the density contributions to the two pressure
products in~\eqref{pkk} and~\eqref{hkk} are now bounded by
\[
C2^{bk}\varepsilon M^{\tau_1/2}
X_{k+2}^{1-\tau_1/2},
\qquad
C2^{2bk}\varepsilon^{\theta_1}M^{1-\theta_2}
X_{k+2}^{(1-\theta_1)/2+\theta_2},
\]
respectively. The energy exponents remain strictly less than
one, by the choices made in that proof. All the remaining
terms are independent of density mass smallness and have the
same sublinear energy exponents as before. Since the radii
stay in $[3/4,7/8]$, inclusion of cylinders bounds $X_{k+1}$
by a fixed multiple of $X_{k+2}$. Consequently, for some
$\theta\in(0,1)$ and $b>0$,
\[
X_k\leq C_M2^{bk}(1+X_{k+2}^{\theta}).
\]
Young's inequality therefore gives, for every $a>0$,
\begin{equation}
X_k\leq aX_{k+2}+C_{M,a}2^{Bk}
\label{eq:bounded-mass-energy-recursion}
\end{equation}
with $B>0$. Choose $a2^{2B}<1$. Suitability and cylinder
inclusion imply $\sup_kX_k<\infty$; this finiteness is used
only to discard the tail in the iteration
\[
X_0\leq a^jX_{2j}
+C_{M,a}\sum_{\ell=0}^{j-1}(a2^{2B})^\ell.
\]
Letting $j\to\infty$ and using the energy interpolation
inequality yields
\begin{equation}
A_{u,\sqrt n,\nabla\sqrt{\tilde c}}(3/4)
+E_{u,\sqrt n,\nabla\sqrt{\tilde c}}(3/4)
+\|n\|_{L^{5/3}(\mathcal Q_{3/4})}
\leq C_M.
\label{eq:bounded-mass-local-energy}
\end{equation}
This is a boundedness estimate, not a small-energy estimate.

\medskip\noindent
\textit{Step 2: a caloric decomposition of the density.}
The density equation is
\[
\partial_t n-\Delta n=-\nabla\cdot F,
\qquad F=n(u+\nabla c).
\]
Since $q'=q/(q-1)<5/3$, H\"older's inequality and
\eqref{eq:bounded-mass-local-energy} give
\begin{equation}
\|F\|_{L^1(\mathcal Q_{3/4})}
\leq\|n\|_{L^{q'}(\mathcal Q_{3/4})}
\|u+\nabla c\|_{L^q(\mathcal Q_{3/4})}
\leq C_M\varepsilon.
\label{eq:bounded-mass-small-flux}
\end{equation}
In the boundary case, extend $n$ evenly across $x_3=0$,
extend $F_1,F_2$ evenly and $F_3$ oddly, and denote the
extensions by $N,F^{\mathrm e}$ on $Q_{3/4}$.
The weak Neumann identity gives
\[
\partial_tN-\Delta N=-\nabla\cdot F^{\mathrm e}
\quad\text{in }\mathcal D'(Q_{3/4}).
\]
Indeed, the sum of a test function and its reflection has
zero normal derivative on the plane and is an admissible
test in that identity. Thus no classical normal trace is
being assumed. In the interior case put $N=n$ and
$F^{\mathrm e}=F$.

Let $a_0=-9/16$, and extend $F^{\mathrm e}$ by zero from
$Q_{3/4}$ to $\mathbb R^3\times(a_0,0)$. Denote the result
by $\widehat F$. With the heat kernel
\[
G(x,t)=(4\pi t)^{-3/2}\exp(-|x|^2/(4t)),\qquad t>0,
\]
define
\[
w(x,t)=-\int_{a_0}^t\int_{\mathbb R^3}
\nabla_xG(x-y,t-s)\cdot\widehat F(y,s)\,dy\,ds.
\]
Then $(\partial_t-\Delta)w=-\nabla\cdot\widehat F$ in
distributions. Since
$\|\nabla G(\cdot,t)\|_{L^1(\mathbb R^3)}\leq Ct^{-1/2}$,
Tonelli's theorem gives
\begin{align}
\int_{a_0}^0\|w(\cdot,t)\|_{L^1(\mathbb R^3)}\,dt
&\leq C\int_{a_0}^0\int_{a_0}^t
(t-s)^{-1/2}\|\widehat F(\cdot,s)\|_{L^1}\,ds\,dt
\nonumber\\
&\leq C\|\widehat F\|_{L^1(\mathbb R^3\times(a_0,0))}
\leq C_M\varepsilon.
\label{eq:bounded-mass-heat-potential}
\end{align}
The function $v=N-w$ is caloric on $Q_{3/4}$. The local
$L^1$-to-$L^\infty$ estimate for caloric functions therefore
implies
\begin{equation}
\|v\|_{L^\infty(Q_{5/8})}
\leq C\|v\|_{L^1(Q_{3/4})}
\leq C M+C_M\varepsilon.
\label{eq:bounded-mass-caloric-part}
\end{equation}
Only the flux has been extended by zero at the spherical
boundary; no artificial boundary condition is imposed on $n$.

\medskip\noindent
\textit{Step 3: small rescaled density mass.}
For every full or boundary half-cylinder
$\mathcal Q_\rho(z)\subset\mathcal Q_{5/8}$, with
$0<\rho\leq1$, the preceding decomposition and $n\geq0$
give
\begin{equation}
\rho^{-3}\int_{\mathcal Q_\rho(z)}n\,dx\,dt
\leq C M\rho^2+C_M\varepsilon\rho^{-3}.
\label{eq:bounded-mass-density-decay}
\end{equation}
Here the $C_M\varepsilon\rho^2$ contribution from
\eqref{eq:bounded-mass-caloric-part} has been absorbed into
the last term. This estimate is uniform in the center.

Let $\eta>0$ be the threshold in Theorem~\ref{main3} for
the equal exponents $(q,q)$ and pressure exponent $\tilde q$.
It is admissible because $5/q<2$ and $F(q,q)=1$.
For scales at most one we use the original upper bound
$M_\phi$ for the rescaled potential gradient.
Choose $0<r\leq1/64$, depending only on $M$ and the fixed
parameters, so that
\[
C M r^2\leq\eta/6.
\]
The constants can be enlarged independently of $r$ so that,
at either radius $\rho=r$ or $\rho=r/8$, the error term in
\eqref{eq:bounded-mass-density-decay} is bounded by
$C_M\varepsilon r^{-3}$.
For the same cylinders, restriction, rescaling, and change of
pressure mean give
\begin{align*}
C^{q,q}_{u,\nabla\sqrt{\tilde c}}(\rho;z)
&\leq C r^{1-5/q}\varepsilon,\\
D_{\tilde q,1}(\rho;z)
&\leq C r^{-1-2/\tilde q}\varepsilon.
\end{align*}
In the second inequality we used, for almost every time,
\[
\int_{\mathcal B_\rho(z)}|p-[p]_{\mathcal B_\rho(z)}|\,dx
\leq2\int_{\mathcal B_\rho(z)}|p-[p]_1|\,dx.
\]
After fixing $r$, choose
\begin{equation}
0<\varepsilon_1\leq
\min\left\{1,\frac{\eta r^3}{6C_M},
\frac{\eta r^{5/q-1}}{3C},
\frac{\eta r^{1+2/\tilde q}}{3C}\right\}.
\label{eq:bounded-mass-threshold-choice}
\end{equation}
For $\varepsilon\leq\varepsilon_1$, every such cylinder of
either selected radius satisfies
\[
C^{q,q}_{u,\nabla\sqrt{\tilde c}}(\rho;z)
+\rho^{-3}\int_{\mathcal Q_\rho(z)}n\,dx\,dt
+D_{\tilde q,1}(\rho;z)\leq\eta.
\]
Thus Theorem~\ref{main3} applies after rescaling.
In particular, it is the small density mass on this smaller
cylinder, rather than the original bound $M$, that enters
the small-energy iteration leading to Proposition~\ref{main1}.

\medskip\noindent
\textit{Step 4: coverage of the asserted region.}
In the boundary case, take any
$z=(x,t)\in\overline{Q_{1/2}^+}$. If $x_3\leq r/4$,
use the boundary cylinder $Q_r^+(x',0,t)$; its half-cylinder
contains $z$ in its spatial interior relative to the closed
half-space. If $x_3>r/4$, use the full cylinder $Q_{r/8}(z)$,
which is contained in the half-space. These cylinders lie
in $Q_{5/8}^+$. In the interior reference case, use
$Q_{r/8}(z)\subset Q_{5/8}$ for every
$z\in\overline{Q_{1/2}}$.
The preceding estimates are uniform for all these centers.
As in the proof of Theorem~\ref{main3}, move terminal times
slightly forward when $t<0$ and use the terminal closure at
$t=0$. The resulting neighborhoods cover the asserted closed
half-cylinder or full cylinder, and a finite subcover gives
the claimed regularity.
Finally, choose the intermediate radius nonincreasing in $M$
and replace $r^{5/q-1}$ in~\eqref{eq:bounded-mass-threshold-choice}
by $r^{\max\{5/q-1,0\}}$ if necessary. Together with the
nondecreasing choice of $C_M$, this makes $\varepsilon_1$
nonincreasing in $M$.

body_md:
Apply Theorem~\ref{main3} with $q=r=10/3$ and $\tilde q=5/3$.
On the unit cylinder,
$\|n\|_{L^1}\leq |\mathcal Q|^{2/5}\|n\|_{L^{5/3}}$.
Choosing $\varepsilon_4$ sufficiently small in terms of the
